jurisdiction.venue: U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York, Brooklyn

headline: Brooklyn Jury Convicts Huawei on 10 Federal Counts After ‘ocsic’ Code Theft and Iran Sanctions Trial
deck: Following a three-month trial before Judge Ann M. Donnelly, Huawei Technologies and three subsidiaries were found guilty of bank fraud, wire fraud, money laundering conspiracy, IEEPA sanctions violations, and trade-secret theft—while winning acquittals on RICO and obstruction.

financials.amount_display: Billions in U.S.-Dollar Clearing & Trade Secrets

street_crime_compare.exec_summary: A Brooklyn federal jury convicted Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. and three subsidiaries on 10 of 12 counts—including bank fraud, wire fraud, Iran sanctions violations, money laundering conspiracy, and trade-secret theft—with sentencing set for Sept. 14, 2027.
street_crime_compare.street_equivalent: Lifting a rival workshop's patented machine arm into a backpack, renaming the blueprint backwards on the cover, and falsifying loan applications to keep the bank credit line open
street_crime_compare.street_sentence: Multi-year federal felony custody plus restitution for individual defendants; corporate defendants face financial penalties at sentencing
